I obviously knew what the administration for communications was involved in, and their main task was to provide secure communications wherever those secure communications were needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would ask for the Court Officer to please call up P2615. Mr. Vujovic, just maybe have a quick look at it and let me know when you're ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the document relates to -- or states that the Serbian MUP provided some Land Rovers with RAKEL radio devices for use in the Krajina SUP in April 1991. Can you explain what the RAKEL radio devices are?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's RAKEL. And it's a very well-known British-based company. They produced professional communications equipment. So this is just a notification to the effect that the communications administration was provided with a vehicle with that equipment and also there are some details of the whole set, of the whole equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. And did this kind of -- the adjusted Land Rovers that you had at Pajzos that you talked about, did they also have these kinds of RAKEL devices?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend says this document refers to April 1991. I may be mistaken, but I really can't see how she came to the conclusion that this document relates to April 1991. The only thing we see on the document itself is 7th of May, 1992. I apologise, Your Honours. Your Honours, I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last year-- a reference to last year is usually to the previous year, Mr. Petrovic. Ms. Friedman, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. So did you have these devices in Pajzos as well?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no need for that. The purpose of this equipment is not the same as the purpose of the equipment at Pajzos. RAKEL devices are used in communications between ourselves. And Pajzos had the equipment that was used to intercept any kind of other people's communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, about halfway down the page, the communications commander who authored the report states: "After approximately two months, there was a need for Land Rover vehicles, and pursuant to an order by Frenk, the chief representative of the Serbian MUP, I dismantled the entire equipment from two of the vehicles and moved them to two Lada Niva vehicles ..." My first question is whether you knew that Franko Simatovic was in the Krajina before being in Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And a little further down, the document states: "The emptied Land Rovers were used to tow mortars and transport the crews in the area of Velika Glava." Mr. Vujovic, you'll agree that this indicates involvement in -- in something other than gathering intelligence.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know if Mr. Franko was involved in something else on the territory. My communication with him, my obligations, the obligations of my administration were to collect intelligence. As for Franko Simatovic, whether he did something else, and when he did it, if he, indeed, was involved in something else, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you testified that when you -- that you arrived Pajzos. Now, did you say -- I believe you said it was 1993. And can you explain how long you stayed there at first?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just a simple working meeting. Now, as to how much time can that take, whether it was an hour or a couple of hours, I can't remember. But I spent perhaps a couple of hours at Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you were never -- is it -- were you never posted there on a more permanent or semi- -- temporary basis?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean me?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean me, personally, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you stated that you returned to Pajzos later. Specifically you said: "I went there in 1994 and 1995, 1996. During that period, I was there twice, I believe. I really don't know exactly." That's at T19601? And I just want to clarify, was it -- if you can provide any more information. When you were there during the two periods, was it, again, just a meeting, or were you there for a little longer?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you misquoted me. I said that I had been at Pajzos, as far as I can remember, only two times. To a question put to me by the Defence, or whoever it was who asked me when that was, I said that it may have been either in 1994 or 1995, or 1996. I am not sure. In any case, I went to Pajzos only twice. Both of the times I attended meetings there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And does that include -- just to revise, then, is this -- it was only two times, even from 1993 when you first joined?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. And was it a whole day each time, or half a day, a couple -- can -- can you give us some indication?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you a minute ago. It could not have been even half a day, let alone a whole day. We're talking perhaps a couple of hours at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So, in total from 1992 when the post was set up until 1996, you were maybe there for a couple of hours in total?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Me, personally. Only a few hours. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So when you said that -- you also said that the post was secured by people in an anti-terrorist unit, or I believe you confirmed that it was the JATD. This was information that you got when you were there or were you told at some other time?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was there, I can't remember the circumstances, but I believe that in a conversation with somebody, I was informed that it was the anti-terrorist unit, our own anti-terrorist unit, that provided security for the facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, Your Honours, can I just have a moment to confer. Okay. Can I please have 65 ter 6535. And I have a hard copy to be handed to the witness. And this should not be broadcast. And just for -- we have only partial translations uploaded as of now. They will be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sir, these are some -- yesterday my colleague Mr. Petrovic showed you a JATD payment list, and you were able to identify three individuals whom you said were engaged in communication activities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a payment list or a payroll. I was shown a document that had to do with the payment of per diems, and these are two different things. And there were two men there who had been involved in that work.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the witness sufficiently clarified, I take it, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: There was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Payment is an ambiguous expression but it is clear what was shown to the witness yesterday. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And as for the two people Judge Orie had questioned further, and, Mr. Vujovic, I don't know if you recall that you also identified an additional person at the -- who was number 1 on the list.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And just right before we get to yours, I'll just -- to these new lists, I'll note for Your Honours that the payment list shown to the witness were -- was Exhibit P458 and it was discussed at T9607 -- sorry, 19607 to 19608, and I would call the Chamber's attention in this respect to Exhibit P441, paragraph, 93, and P454, page 23, as it relates to the evidence of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vujovic, what you see in front of you are seven payment lists on which you appear from 1993 to 1995, which the Prosecution received pursuant to a Request for Assistance from the Serbian MUP. Now these payment lists in which you appear are not JATD payment lists; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither confirm nor deny that because, as far as I can see, all these payment lists are personalised. There are names and surnames there. Now, whether somebody is a member of the JATD, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a problem with the presentation of this document by my learned friend; because when we look at the bottom of this page, we see something that is different from what she seems to suggest through her question. I don't want to say what that is in front of the witness. But the document is not the way she had interpreted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, most important is that the witness looks at what the Prosecution wants to show. And, Ms. Friedman, apparently, there's a problem in the way you described the document. If you would try to do that as neutral as possible, it would be appreciated. A list containing names and amounts of money, because that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it is entitled: List of payroll documents to be entered. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you read literally from the document, then Mr. Petrovic will not have any concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, for the time-periods that were paid for, you were not specifically connected to JATD operations; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question seems to be a bit unclear to me. Linking this list to whether I was part of the JATD, well, the JATD was established in 1993. I've already explained that we, as the 7th Administration, as far as our obligations towards the JATD were concerned, they were minimal, and they ended at the level of some kind of logistic support. So that is the beginning and the end of it, as far as the 7th Administration and the JATD is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, that was -- that was my question. It wasn't saying that you were part of the JATD on the basis of this list. It was quite the opposite, saying that this is a generic list that does not say anything about an anti-terrorist unit. It's a list of the Serbian DB, where you worked, the 8th department which dispensed funds and payment, and you're on this list, and I take it from this list that your payment here is not for activities in connection to the JATD?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please. This is already the second time that my colleague is repeating that this list has nothing to do with the ATD. Please take a look at number 20 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman. But ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you said it does not say anything, that might be not entirely correct in view of what Mr. Petrovic just said. But why not put the questions in a very practical way. That is, Mr. Vujovic, whether he has any recollection of this amount of money, which was apparently recorded here as either to be paid to him or paid to him and in what connection that was. Because that's what apparently you're seeking to establish.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I think I'll just take a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I think Mr. Petrovic also was referring to something else on the list, not what -- at least not what appears in the transcript, and I think it's amounting to testimony, and that I can put my case to the witness and we can discuss it further afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But the case is this: That you were on this list, that you were paid by the 8th Administration, as can you see on this list, and that it was not within the category of ATD or JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is the following: This is a list that was generated by the 8th Administration for the sake of payment. It has to do with the payment of certain monies. I recognised some of the persons on this list. The dominant motive is to have a justification for the money that was paid out. Now, whether there was someone from some particular organisational unit, all of it is mixed up here. I looked at it very carefully on each and every page; because, basically, the 8th Administration when it is paying per diems, it doesn't really have to particularly focus on whether a person is from this or that administration. It simply has to do with the right of any employee to have a per diem if they travel. I really cannot say. I mean, I just knew the deputy commander and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And ATD actually appears separately on this list at number 25. Are any of the other individuals that you recognise on the first list people that you knew to be providing assistance to the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I could give comments only in respect of persons from my administration, whether any of them assisted the JATD at some point in time, in the context that I already referred to. Of course, I cannot say anything about others. So, from my administration, it is number 17, myself, and then 18, Miladinovic, Vlatko; and then that person -- is also from the 7th Administration; 19 is Ramus, Slobodan, also from my administration. Now, on the basis of what we are on this list, this -- and this particular date, we did something in September 1993 and we received per diems on account of that. I mean, I'm looking at all these names. This is totally mixed up. I mean, all these different structures. And it's certain that not all the persons on this list -- I mean, this is just payment of per diems. It is not whether it has to do with the JATD or something else. It's just per diems. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if your services for which you were paid had been specifically at that time-period for the benefit or on behalf of the JATD, you would have likely been listed on a JATD payment list specifically rather than this more general Serbian DB payment list; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object. The witness has been testifying for two days, and he has not provided any services to the JATD. What is this question based on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're giving evidence, Mr. Petrovic. He has been testifying for two days, and he has not provided -- that's improper. The Prosecution is entitled to explore with this witness lists of payment issued by the 8th Administration on which the witness, his name appears, separate from an entry which refers to the anti-terrorist operations. You can further re -- in re-examination, you can deal with the matter in further detail. Please proceed, Ms. Friedman. But it would be appreciated if you put clear questions to the witness, rather than to -- whether he would have likely been on other lists or that -- that's -- try to put questions such as whether he remembers that this money was paid to him, and what he may have done for that on the 20 -- in that period of time, what it was that he got daily travel allowance for. Then we focus on the facts, rather than on how the administration could have been different, if the situation would have been different, and that's not very helpful. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of where you were posted or what you were doing during these time-periods?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't remember. I'm on several of these lists. Every time I travelled out of town meant that I was entitled to a per diem. It wasn't only me. Any employee of the service had that entitlement. Now I really cannot say. I mean, I really cannot say what this travel was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For my understanding, Ms. Friedman, a 928 million, that refers to what currency, dinar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dinars. Dinars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication, otherwise we may have ways to find out, what approximately 928 million dinars was in September 1993 in deutschemarks because that was the currency you used in practice, from what I understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I cannot recall. I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the amount you got per diem when you were travelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our per diems were very small. The order of magnitude was, say, let's put it in euro if that's easier now, 20 or 25 euro, present-day euro. That was the per diem then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was your salary at that time in present-day euros? Well, let's say, per month.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I'm trying to remember. Well, it certainly wasn't more than, say, 500, 600 euro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the per diems, if you would be travelling, would be approximately the same as your salary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what you're saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there's a per diem, which literally means "per day," if that is 20 or 25 euro, if you would in a month be travelling all the time, that would be 20 -- a little bit over 20 times 20 to 25 euros which amounts to anything between 450 and 600 euros, so approximately the same as your regular salary was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But if it would be an absence of 20 days, or more, of permanent absence, well, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you said it was very small. It was approximately the same amount being absent. You may proceed, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to tendered these lists into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Lists. Yeah. Madam Registrar, the number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6535 will receive number P3161, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I hear of no objections. P3161 is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, you described how, when Mr. Stanisic was removed in 1998 -- well, you referred to it as a shake-up, but it was also when Mr. Stanisic was removed from office, and at that point you were offered -- you were removed from your position and offered a different one. Now, do you believe that that happened because of your affiliation with Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In services of this kind, generally speaking, when the chief of service is changed, especially in such a forceful manner, it is only natural that the package would include dismissal of the head of department for operative equipment. That would be the only reason. I don't see any other reason in the context of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you refuse the new position out of an allegiance?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal motive for resigning was my thinking of -- along the following lines, because the replacement had been carried out in such a way and the people who were brought in were simply people I was convinced could not bring the results that a state service is supposed to yield. The key factor -- or, rather, the camel that -- the straw that broke the camel's back was when Rade Markovic was brought in. I can say that straight away. He held this short briefing with the chiefs of departments, and he said that everyone should keep their jobs for the time being, and he ended the meeting with the following words. This is verbatim: I expect full loyalty from you to the president, the state, and the party. All of us who had worked in the previous period, while Jovica Stanisic headed the service, were taken aback, astounded to hear the chief of service stay -- say at the very beginning that he would require that from the people who would stay on, full loyalty to the president, state, and party. Which party? I personally took this -- I mean, it wasn't only me, but I personally took this as a terrible degradation of the service itself because absolutely in the previous period - and I underline this word, "absolutely" - we had not been linked to any party whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, I don't know if you're aware, there was a report in February in 2002 of a "Blic" source that said that you were a person who still maintained some power from behind the scenes, and it mentioned only four people: Stanisic, Simatovic, Milorad Ulemek and you. Do you know why you were singled out to be on this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the witness could be shown and the rest of us could be shown the report so we all know what we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: At 65 ter 6530. It's a second-hand report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I just want to know if the witness had heard of this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend said that it had been published in the "Blic" newspaper. I am interested to see the original from the "Blic" daily. Because what we are looking at the moment is some computer-generated copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's what you said, Ms. Friedman, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman said that it's a second-hand reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it's just in the last paragraph and it just says a "Blic" news source. I did not call it up or intend to tender it, actually, because it is only the basis for my question. I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether -- of course, the witness could comment on it, whether it was or was not published in "Blic," whether that's a reliable reference is another matter. But I think that for Ms. Friedman it's not most important whether it was in "Blic" or in the "New York Herald," or wherever, but that this kind information was published. Could you tell us where this was published, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: This is in the VIP news source which is a collection quoting other -- other news source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm familiar with VIP. But if --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Published in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's the source, Mr. Petrovic. Please proceed, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was just -- Mr. Vujovic, do you -- were you aware of this before? Do you know what could have caused this rumour?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this before. And a perfunctory look tells me that the context is co-operation between Serbia and Israel. The author of this text says that a lobby was set up to do something with regard to the co-operation between Israel and Serbia and other things. Me, personally, I think this is sheer nonsense. What year did you say that that was published? 2000?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2002. I was assistant chief of the RDB Serbia. I was appointed to that position with Prime Minister Djindjic's consents. So this story is sheer nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to note for Your Honours that actually concludes my questions, but on Pajzos, since we expected the witness to have spent more time there but didn't, I'm just going to refer Your Honours to the evidence demonstrating the continuity of the Serbian DB unit and it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you -- at this moment, are you cross-examining the witness or are you arguing what, although the witness could not testify about -- what we should look at.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would like to put on the record six documents to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that that should not be done. If you say the witness could not confirm this and then -- either you may draw our attention to what is in evidence in relation to this evidence but not a continuity of Pajzos in general terms. That's seems to be inappropriate to bring to our attention now. I'm not saying that it would, under all circumstances, be inappropriate in the future or when we will hear argument.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no further questions. Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just a few questions. It will take me no more than a few minutes to put them, but I believe my learned friend from the other Defence team has also got a few questions. But I believe if I start now, we can finish today, in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was hoping for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Then we have to do it tomorrow. Mr. Petrovic, I'm always a bit suspicious if you say that you can finish in four minutes. I hope you will not blame me for that. But let's see how far we come. Four minutes are left. Mr. Vujovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's me first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's you first. Yes, you are right. That's -- my apologies. Four minutes for you -- three and a half by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just, can I pick up quickly on your alleged affiliation with Mr. Stanisic. You were shown a document where you were given a financial reward, and it actually says statement of reasons: The deputy head of the department has proposed to give the financial reward. Who was the deputy head of the department at the time who proposed to give -- or at the time. Leave it there.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it said either assistant chief or deputy chief. Let's be precise. I believe that I read the text well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's -- let's have it up on the screen. 06527, please, I think not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps we should move into private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We can see there underneath the statement saying statement of reasons. And it states that the deputy head of the department has proposed the financial reward, and that's ... The English translation says "deputy."

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What does the -- how do you read it, please?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Assistant head.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's what I'm reading in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who was the assistant head in May of 1998, please?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, the assistant head of the department for equipment was Vojkin Cvetkovic, who was my immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, my learned friend also suggested that you left your post because of your affiliation with Stanisic. Am I correct that when Stanisic left and when you left, many members of the State Security Service were replaced by members of Milosevic's political party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right. Mr. Stanisic was removed from his position on the 27th of October, 1998. And I, myself, was removed on the 30th of October, 1998. That meeting took place at night, starting at about 1000 p.m. at -- that same people, together with me, three other heads of services were removed from their positions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it was day or night is -- was not part of the question. But we have to conclude for the day. Tomorrow we'll need a little bit more time, Mr. Vujovic. I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way about your testimony. And we adjourn until tomorrow, the 24th of May, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of May, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
